keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user already has an up-to-date prescription determines whether obtaining one is a prerequisite step before ordering.
The sunglasses may be for the user themselves or for someone else (e.g., a child or partner), which affects prescription details, frame sizing, and who reviews fit.
Prescription sunglasses range from under $50 to over $500; budget directly narrows which retailers and lens/frame options are viable.
Frame style, colour, and material (e.g., sporty wraparound vs. classic wayfarers) heavily influence which sites and filters to use when browsing.
Lens choices — tint, polarised, photochromic, UV coating — vary by retailer and add-on cost, so knowing the priority shapes which options to select at checkout.
Primary use (daily driving, outdoor sports, beach/travel) determines how much lens performance matters vs. aesthetics, and narrows the right product category.
Understanding what a successful purchase looks like — fastest delivery, lowest price, best return/try-on policy, or trusted brand — determines which retailer to prioritise.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to purchase a new pair of prescription sunglasses through an online retailer.

questions.title: Do you have a current, valid prescription ready?
questions.description: Determine whether the user already has an up-to-date prescription from an optometrist, or whether getting one is a required first step.

questions.title: Who are the sunglasses being ordered for?
questions.description: Establish whether the sunglasses are for the user or for someone else, which affects prescription details and sizing.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for this purchase?
questions.description: Identify a budget range to narrow down viable retailers and frame/lens combinations.

questions.title: What frame style or aesthetic are you going for?
questions.description: Understand style preferences — shape, colour, material — to guide browsing and filtering on retailer sites.

questions.title: Do you need polarised, tinted, or any specific lens feature?
questions.description: Clarify lens priorities such as polarisation, photochromic capability, or UV coatings to ensure the right add-ons are selected at checkout.

questions.title: What will you mainly use these sunglasses for?
questions.description: Identify the primary use case — driving, sport, casual wear, beach — to match the right product category and lens performance level.

questions.title: What matters most: price, speed of delivery, or return policy?
questions.description: Determine the user's top priority to decide which online retailer to recommend or use first.
